 JUDGMENT Heard Sri.M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri.H.M.Dharigond, learned counsel for respondent No.3.
2.

Insurance Company is in appeal challenging the validity of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.443/2013 dated 22.01.2016 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T.,
Bailhongal,
3.

sentences.text:
Brief facts of the case are as under:
Dependants of Sri.Basavaraj Ramappa Tangoji namely Smt.Kallawwa and Kumar Sanju, who are the mother and minor son, laid a claim under Section 163A of Motor Vehicles Act involving a motorcycle bearing No.KA- 24/K-8878 and Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA.24/T-6578.
4.

Since the deceased was the driver/rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-24/K-8878, Tribunal taking note NC: 2024:KHC-D:3654 of the charge sheet being filed against both the rider of the motorcycle and driver of Maxima Goods vehicle, apportioned the compensation amount to be paid in 50:50 ratio and the compensation amount in a sum of Rs.4,48,000/- is awarded as per the second schedule to Motor Vehicles Act.
5. Being aggrieved by the apportioning 50% of the compensation amount to be paid by the Insurance Company of the motorcycle, Insurance Company is in appeal.

sentences.text: Sri .M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel for the appellant, reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum vehemently contended that since the rider of the motorcycle is the owner of the motorcycle, he cannot be allowed to claim the compensation amount from his own insurer, on account of his own wrong and sought for allowing the appeal.
Per contra, Sri.H.M.Dharigond, learned counsel for respondent No.3 supported the impugned judgment.
Claimants though served with the notice, remained absent.
8. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

9. On such perusal of the material on record, there is payment of additional sum of Rs.50/- covering the personal accident claim insofar as Insurance Policy obtained on behalf of the deceased in respect of the motorcycle.
10. Therefore, out of Rs.2,24,000/- payable by the Insurance Company, Rs.1,00,000/- is to be borne by the Insurance Company and remaining Rs.1,24,000/- is to be borne by the owner himself.
11. Therefore, a modification is needed insofar as liability of the appellant/Insurance Company is concerned by exonerating the liability to the extent of Rs.1,24,000/-.

Accordingly, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part as against 50% liability of the appellant/Insurance Company, Insurance Company is liable to pay Rs.1,00,000/-
with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
ii. Balance sum of Rs.1,24,000/- is concerned is to be borne by the deceased himself,
being the owner of the motorcycle and to that extent liability of the Insurance Company stands exonerated.
iii. Amount is deposited is transmitted to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
